source_evidence: Surrender charges will reduce the value and the return of your investment.
answer: Withdrawing money from an indexed annuity early can have two separate effects. If you withdraw before the end of an index-measuring period, you may not receive all of that period’s return. If you withdraw some or all of your money during the contract’s surrender period, you may also have to pay a surrender charge. The surrender period typically lasts six to ten years or longer after purchase, and the charge reduces the annuity’s value and return. Check the contract to understand how withdrawals and surrender charges apply.
